key_points.details: Rick (Engineering Manager at DAS), Leo (Manager), Alicia (Data), Luis (Computer Engineer), Hiram (Software Engineer), Julio (Software Engineer)

key_points.point: SSIS jobs are tightly coupled and fragile
key_points.details: Jobs drop and truncate tables then rebuild from scratch. If anything crashes, entire tables go missing. Jobs run on predetermined intervals with dependencies on previous jobs

key_points.point: Jobs frequently fail and require constant manual fixes
key_points.details: 3-4 data engineers in India constantly fix failures. One job has never run successfully. Failures happen randomly and are fixed without documentation or notification
Created a week ago to track job status, failure rates, and success rates. Shows current running jobs and upcoming jobs

key_points.point: Job descriptions are unclear and poorly documented
key_points.details: Some job purposes unknown. AI was used to determine descriptions because getting information from engineers is difficult

key_points.point: SQL code is in repository with some AWS integration
key_points.details: SQL committed to repo. AWS monitors SFTP for new files, pulls them, and triggers SSIS jobs to process records into database

key_points.point: Multiple data sources including customer SFTPs
key_points.details: SFTP sometimes on company end, sometimes on customer dealership end. AWS and SSIS handle file processing and database loading

key_points.point: Multiple databases across EC2 and RDS instances
key_points.details: Main SSIS jobs run on EC2. Two RDS instances handle webhook data from emails/SMS. Mautic (open source) runs on RDS for segmentation and emailing

key_points.point: System is brittle with unclear failure points
key_points.details: When jobs break, it's unclear where the failure occurred. Requires 3 engineers to keep running daily. Very expensive to maintain

key_points.point: AWS Glue considered but not a real solution
key_points.details: Considered moving to serverless AWS Glue to downsize databases, but this just moves the problem to cloud without addressing underlying architectural issues

key_points.point: 12-year-old legacy system with accumulated technical debt
key_points.details: Application changed hands multiple times. No cleanup of old artifacts. Unused databases like BirdBath and Digital Bundle still exist but not deleted due to fear of breaking something

key_points.point: ETL jobs previously took over 24 hours
key_points.details: Optimizations and indexing have been applied to improve processing time

action_items.action: Investigate and document why one SSIS job has never run successfully
action_items.context: One job in the SSIS pipeline has a 0% success rate and it's unclear why it's still in the system

action_items.action: Implement better monitoring and alerting system for SSIS job failures
action_items.context: Data engineers are silently fixing failures without notifying the team; need visibility into what's breaking and how it's being fixed

action_items.action: Get accurate job descriptions from engineers for all SSIS jobs
action_items.context: Several job descriptions are unknown or were guessed using AI; need accurate documentation

action_items.action: Evaluate AWS Glue as alternative to current SSIS infrastructure
action_items.context: Team has been considering serverless approach to reduce database maintenance and costs

action_items.action: Audit and delete unused databases (BirdBath, Digital Bundle, etc.)
action_items.context: 12-year-old application has accumulated unused databases that haven't been cleaned up due to uncertainty about their purpose

action_items.action: Refactor tightly coupled SSIS jobs to reduce fragility
action_items.context: Current architecture drops and rebuilds tables from scratch, causing data loss if any job crashes; requires 3-4 engineers to maintain daily
